facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Since the fourteenth century Sanchi remained deserted and uncared for till 1818 when General Taylor rediscovered the site.
facts.text: The deserted and overgrown ruins of Sanchi were rediscovered by British cavalry officer General Henry Taylor in 1818.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In 1822, Captain Johnson, Assistant Political Agent in Bhopal, opened up Stupa 1 from top to bottom on one side, thus leaving a great breach which resulted in the collapse of the West Gateway and a part of the enclosing balustrade.
facts.source_name: John Marshall, A Guide to Sanchi
facts.text: In 1822, Captain Johnson breached the Great Stupa from top to bottom on its western side while digging for buried treasure, causing the western gateway to collapse.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: They also sank a shaft at the centre of Stupa 1, which, however, failed to yield any relics.
facts.text: Alexander Cunningham and Captain F. C. Maisey sank a vertical shaft through the centre of the Great Stupa in 1851 but found no relic casket.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The relics of Sariputra and Maha Moggalana, the two foremost disciples of the Buddha, were found by Colonel Cunningham in 1851 in this stupa, enshrined at the centre of the dome on the level of the terrace.
facts.text: Alexander Cunningham discovered inscribed stone relic caskets bearing bone fragments of the Buddha's chief disciples, Sariputta and Maha-Moggallana, inside Stupa 3 at Sanchi in 1851.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Sir John Marshall established an archaeological museum in 1919, which was later transformed into the present site museum at Sanchi.
facts.text: Archaeological Survey of India Director General Sir John Marshall directed the comprehensive restoration of Sanchi's monuments and reconstructed the fallen gateways between 1912 and 1919.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: When he was heir-apparent and was journeying as Viceroy to Ujjain, he is said to have halted at Vidisha (10 kilometers from Sanchi), and there married the daughter of a local banker. She was called Devi and later gave Ashoka two sons, Ujjeniya and Mahendra, and a daughter Sanghamitta.
facts.text: The Mahavamsa records that Ashoka married Devi, the daughter of a merchant in nearby Vidisha, who later established a monastery on the hill of Chetiyagiri.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: He erected the Great Stupa (Stupa 1) here after redistribution of mortal remains of Lord Buddha for erecting several stupas all over the country in order to spread Buddhism.
facts.text: Popular Buddhist tradition holds that Emperor Ashoka recovered the Buddha's relics from seven ancient mounds and redistributed them into eighty-four thousand stupas across the realm.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In the first century BC the Andhra-Satavahanas, who had extended their sway over the eastern Malwa, caused the elaborately carved gateways to Stupa 1. The Great Stupa of Sanchi displays an austere grandeur and the exquisite carvings of the doorway depict in detail the significant episodes and miracles from Lord Buddha's life and events depicted in the Buddhist Jataka stories.
facts.text: Four intricately sculpted sandstone gateways added to Stupa 1 during the 1st century BCE portray Buddhist Jataka stories such as the Chaddanta and Vessantara tales.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Divyavadana, a Buddhist Sanskrit work from the early centuries of the Common Era, describes the Brahmin ruler Pushyamitra Shunga as a great persecutor of Buddhists.
facts.text: The Sanskrit chronicle Divyavadana asserts that the Shunga ruler Pushyamitra Shunga waged an extermination campaign against Buddhist shrines and monastics in northern India.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: He also theorized that the Sanchi stupa was vandalized in 2nd century BCE (that is, during Pushyamitra's reign), before being rebuilt on a larger scale.
facts.text: Historians disagree on whether 2nd-century BCE damage to Ashoka's brick stupa reflects targeted persecution by Pushyamitra Shunga or ordinary weathering followed by peaceful Shunga-period expansion.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Susan Huntington of Ohio State University is of the opinion that most of the reliefs in Bharhut, Sanchi and Amaravati represent worship at sacred Buddhist sites and not aniconic representations pointing to the Buddha.
facts.source_name: Art Journal (Susan L. Huntington) / Ars Orientalis (Vidya Dehejia)
facts.text: Scholars disagree over whether the empty thrones, wheels, and footprints on Sanchi's gateways represent aniconic surrogates for the Buddha or denote sacred pilgrimage sites and devotional monuments.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Standing roughly 100 feet high with a base diameter of around 350 feet, it is significantly larger than Sanchi Stupa, which measures 54 feet in height and 120 feet in diameter.
facts.text: The preserved Great Stupa structure measures approximately 16.4 metres in height and roughly 36.6 metres in dome diameter.
